Design update

What changed on the Margo site

A visual before-and-after. The words, services and contact details are untouched — this pass was about how the page reads: less clutter, clearer hierarchy, and a consistent look from top to bottom.

−30%shorter on desktop
−24%shorter on phones
7clutter items removed
4label styles, down from 16

The opening screen

The first thing a visitor sees. Previously three separate things competed for attention before they reached the headline.

  • Removed the small “Personal Financial Advisory” badge above the headline — the headline says it better.
  • The headline now sits on one line instead of breaking in two.
  • The two buttons now share the width evenly rather than stopping short and leaving a gap.
  • The three pillars moved above the buttons, so you read the promise before the ask.
  • Removed the “Ready to talk?” strip from the quote card — the same contact options appear further down.

On a phone

The headline had shrunk so much on small screens that it barely outranked the paragraph beneath it. It now leads the page the way it does on a desktop.

  • The headline is noticeably larger and clearly the first thing you read.
  • Body text stays at a comfortable reading size — it had been squeezed smaller to make room.

Services

Six service cards and the heading above them. The cards carried a lot of furniture that wasn’t earning its place.

  • Removed the explanatory paragraph on the right of the heading.
  • The heading now fits on one line.
  • Each card is simpler: title and icon on one row, category underneath, and the “Read Approach” footer bar removed — the whole card was always clickable.
  • The “Unsure where to start?” banner is now gold rather than black, with a dark button so it still stands out.

The jargon translator

The three explanation boxes were styled inconsistently, and the first one was red — which on a website usually means something has gone wrong.

  • The “How banks & industry express it” box is no longer red. It now uses the same neutral cream as the “traditional sales” column above, so it reads as the industry’s voice rather than an error.
  • All three boxes now match in size, spacing and text. Emphasis comes from the background colour instead: cream for the jargon, gold for Margo’s plain-English version, dark for why it matters.
  • Removed the instruction line above the list — the list is self-explanatory.
  • The selected term is easier to spot, with a gold marker down its edge.

Throughout the page

Smaller corrections applied everywhere rather than in one place.

  • Tighter spacing around dividing lines. Every divider on the site now has the same breathing room; previously they ranged from generous to very generous.
  • Smaller buttons. They were oversized relative to the text around them. Now two consistent sizes across the whole site.
  • Consistent small-capital labels. There were sixteen slightly different styles for what is essentially one thing; now four, each with a clear job.
  • The header’s “Get Started” button now hides while the one in the opening screen is visible, so two identical buttons never compete. It fades back in as you scroll down.
  • Removed the WhatsApp button from the header — WhatsApp is still on the floating button, in Contact, and in the footer.
  • Removed the “No pressure. Just clarity.” panel at the end of Contact.
Nothing was removed from what you offer. Every service, price band, contact route and piece of guidance is still on the page. The removals were repeated labels, instructions the design already made obvious, and decoration — not content.
